Isolated contract reviewer for PR #21559 (card #21464, stage 2 / S-list), written 2026-10-03T07:24Z. Inputs: the card body and its ten comments (triage `5961300594`, the stage-1 claim `5962381903`, dev reports `5963737459` / `5964076083` / `5966618272`, seat answers `5963787404` / `5966636964`, the ACCEPT `5964211944`, the landing `5964405985`, the stage-2 claim `5965611825`); PR #21559 (body, the 9-file list, the net diff against `main`, +679 / -45, the docs-drift bot comment `5966588436`); the 34 check-runs on this head; the precedents (PR #21463's record `5961282483`; PR #21502's records `5963877733` and `5964200665`, landed `529d9711fb`); and objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `89cad75d55`, read file by file through the contents API: `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, `columnSpellingDiagnostics.ts`, `resolveBulkActions.ts`, `inline-edit-options.ts`, `plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `KanbanImpl.tsx`, `KanbanBoardCore.tsx`, `types.ts`, `plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx`, `components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx`, `types/src/complex.ts`, and the fixtures `gridGroupingMembers-8071`, `serverGroupedSelectIdentity-11105`, `inlineEditPersistence`. objectstack's `view.zod.ts` was read at the head through `git show`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Gate verdicts on this head, as they stood at 07:23Z:** 34 check-runs — 31 success · 0 failure · 1 in progress (`Test Core (1/6)`) · 2 skipped by design (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`). The other five `Test Core` shards, `Lint & Repo Gates`, all four `Type Check` jobs, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, both Part-of gates and the three `Dogfood` gates are success. An in-progress shard is read as in progress, not as a pass. The verdict below is a contract judgment and does not rest on it.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. `object-grid` `columns` → `ListViewSchema.shape.columns` by reference — WRONG AS SHIPPED; the member is held under the seat's own test.** The shape itself matches the read: `normalizeColumns` (`ObjectGrid.tsx:819-830`) dispatches the whole array on its first entry (all strings or all `ListColumn` objects), the summary memo (`:3170-3177`) and the draw path (`:3435-3443`, `resolvesToDataColumn` in `columnSpellingDiagnostics.ts:83-88`) keep only an entry with a non-empty string `field`, the retired `accessorKey` / `header` spellings and a `{ name }` entry draw nothing and are named by the diagnostic (`columnSpellingDiagnostics.ts:76-79`, `:124-142`), and every `ListColumnSchema` member is read in the path-A column literal (`:3664-3690`: `field`, `label`, `width`, `align`, `sortable`, `resizable`, `pinned`, `wrap`, `type`, `link`, `action`, `prefix`, with `hidden` in the filter and `summary` in `useColumnSummary`). `editable` on a column is indeed not read: that literal carries no `editable`, the enrichment at `:4365-4373` starts from it (`{ ...col }` of the EMITTED column, not the authored one) and only ever forces `false` for a non-editable field, and `data-table.tsx:2521` reads the emitted value — so the authored `{ field: 'name', editable: false }` in `inlineEditPersistence.test.tsx:68` is dropped, as the dev says. **But `options` IS read from an authored column at the pin.** The group-header formatter (`ObjectGrid.tsx:2978-3041`, `groupValueFormatter`) does `normalizeColumns(schema.columns)`, finds the authored entry whose `field` is the grouping field (`:2997-2998`), and reads `colOverride?.options || objectDefField?.options` (`:3001`) — the column's own `options` WIN over the object field's — into the per-value label map the group headers draw (`:3021-3030`). objectui pins that as behaviour, not as a drop: `gridGroupingMembers-8071.test.tsx:33-42` ("the memo reads `columns[].options`, which is not among `ListColumn`'s fourteen declared members … while this renderer honours it … pinned below AS BEHAVIOUR and reported as a finding, not repaired here"), `:260-283` (an authored `options: [{ value: 'won', label: 'Closed Won' }, …]` makes the headers read `Closed Lost` / `Closed Won`, with a no-`options` control reading `lost` / `won`), and `:285-301` (`order` sorts by those rendered labels). Those are the 2 `options` values the dev's census refused, filed under "16 column keys the grid never reads … No authored-column read names either key". That sentence is wrong for `options`: it is a value the renderer draws, authored on an `object-grid` column, in a fixture written to pin that it is honoured — a working writer by the test the seat set in `5966636964` ("If the review finds any renderer path at the pin that reads either key from an authored `object-grid` column, that member's narrowing is held (option C for `columns`), and a fix round keeps it in the pin's ledger"). That is also the shape stage 1 held kanban `conditionalFormatting` on (`5963787404` §2): objectui fixtures author a value the renderer reads. That the list view's own door already refuses `options` (strict `ListColumnSchema`) and that objectui's own header calls the read a `declared != enforced` split to retire are the arguments for the ruling, not a licence to ship past the caveat ("reported, not shipped silently"; dispatch A3 "do not ship that member's narrowing"). Consequences for the fix round: `object-grid` `columns[]` returns to the enumeration pin's ledger as `held-for-decision` (the kind still exists; its reader is `ObjectGrid.tsx:2158` and `:2997-3001`), its cases leave the companion pin (§1 two, §2 six, §3 one), and the four texts that assert the grid never reads `options` are corrected: the `columns` docblock (`component.zod.ts`, "a key the grid never reads (`editable`, `options`)"), the changeset's FROM → TO row ("a column key the grid never reads, such as `editable` or `options` — delete the key"), its "Who is affected" paragraph, and the PR body's A3 list. The renderer-side read is the objectui finding objectui's own test already names; the seat decides whether it is carded there (as objectstack-ai/objectui#11522 was for kanban) before the member is typed.

**2. `object-grid` `fields` → `z.array(z.string())` — RIGHT.** The seat's second test ("if a draw path reads an object entry there") is not met. The draw path reads names only: `fieldsToShow = schemaFields` (`:3968-3969`) then `objectSchema.fields?.[fieldName]` with `if (!field) return;` (`:4012-4014`), and the inline-data path (`:3875-3885`) likewise emits `accessorKey: fieldName`. The one place an object entry is read is the fetch projection (`:2583-2589`, `columnIdentity`) and the `$expand` harvest (`:2786-2789`) — the `serverGroupedSelectIdentity-11105` fix, whose own header (`:9-31`) and cast (`:127-132`: "`ObjectGridSchema.fields` is declared `string[]`, and this is the object-entry node the grid receives anyway") say it exercises the node `ListView` hands the grid at run time, not an authored page. Those 3 refused values are that hand-off. No list view declares the member; the renderer's declared type is `string[]`.

**3. `object-grid` `selection` → `ListViewSchema.shape.selection` (`SelectionConfigSchema.optional()`) — RIGHT.** The grid reads `schema.selection?.type` with presence-enables and `type: 'none'` as the explicit off (`:4799-4812`, objectui#9837 A-prime). Observation, carried: the shared def defaults `type` to `none`, so `{ selection: {} }` PARSES to `{ type: 'none' }` (the companion pin §1 asserts exactly that) while the raw bag means ON at the grid; the default lives in parsed output only, the list view door has carried it since the def was declared, objectui#9837 holds the question, and the member docblock records it. Not a defect of this diff.

**4. `object-grid` `selectable` → `boolean | 'single' | 'multiple'` — RIGHT.** Read only when `selection` is absent (`:4813-4815`), handed to the table as `selectable: selectionMode` (`:5333`); `resolveSelectionMode` (`data-table.tsx:637-648`) honours `'single'`, treats falsy as off, and any other truthy value as multiple. The declared set is the table prop's declared type. `'none'`, which the table tolerates "verbatim from raw SDUI JSON" on its own door, is refused here with a lossless rewrite (`false`), and the census authors no `'none'` (2 values, both parse). No working writer refused.

**5. `object-grid` `rowActions` → by reference, `string[]` — RIGHT.** `:1834-1835` reads `Array.isArray(schema.rowActions) ? schema.rowActions : []` typed `string[]`; `edit` / `delete` select the generic entries.

**6. `object-grid` `bulkActions` / `batchActions` → `ListViewSchema.shape.bulkActions`, one def for both — RIGHT.** `:4763` reads `schema.batchActions ?? schema.bulkActions`, filters by `String(a).toLowerCase() !== 'delete'` and folds names through `resolveBulkActions` (its contract, `resolveBulkActions.ts:10`, `:45`: "`bulkActions: string[]` — bare action names"); a `{ name }` entry is the def vocabulary (`bulkActionDefs`) and the two refused values are the fixtures asserting the skip. One capability, one accept set; neither spelling retired, which the direction does not ask for.

**7. `object-kanban` `columns` → all strings, or all lanes `{ id, title, cards?, limit?, className?, collapsed? }` (module-private strict `ObjectKanbanLaneSchema`, `cards[]` a loose object with `id` and `title`) — RIGHT.** `effectiveColumns` (`ObjectKanban.tsx:1161-1188`) dispatches on the first entry and uses a string list only with no `groupBy` (`:1179-1186`); `bucketCardsIntoColumns` (`index.tsx:129-158`) reads `id` and `cards` (`col.cards || []`, so `cards` optional requires no more than the read); `KanbanImpl.tsx` reads `limit` (`:540`, `:591`), `className` (`:568`), `collapsed` (`:742`), `title` and `cards`. The member census over the three files finds `id`, `title`, `cards`, `limit`, `className`, `collapsed` and nothing else. objectui's own `KanbanColumn` (`types/src/complex.ts:126-171`) declares exactly those six, with `color` a RETIRED tombstone ("zero `column.color` read sites"), which the lane's `color` guidance naming `className` mirrors; `KanbanCard` (`:69-121`) declares `id: string; title: string` plus `[key: string]: any`, which is the loose object. `limit` positive-int refuses `0`, which the read treats as no limit (`column.limit && …`); no writer authors it. The one refused value (a lane `color`, `objectKanbanColumnMembers-8071`) is the tombstoned key.

**8. `object-calendar` `calendar` → `ListViewSchema.shape.calendar` (`CalendarConfigSchema.optional()`) — RIGHT.** `getCalendarConfig` (`ObjectCalendar.tsx:294-298`) returns the block as the config; every read destructures exactly the five bindings (`:857`, `:1056`, `:1141`, `:1342-1343`); `startDateField` required is the read (`[startDateField]` keys every event). The retired `dateField` / `endField` aliases were never read off `calendar` (the flat spellings at `:309-317` are the other rung), and the 2 refused values are the alias-refusal fixture.

**9. The enumeration pin.** Nine `staged` lines and the `list-family` stage leave; `no-reader` leaves with no remaining user (its one line went with `ai:chat_window` in PR #21531); one `records` line is added for `columns[].cards[].*`, the loose object's catchall the walk reaches through the union arm — honest (`KanbanCard`'s `[key: string]: any`). The census-equals-ledger construction stands from record `5963877733` ①2. With ①1 held, the fix round re-adds `object-grid` `columns[]` as `held-for-decision`. **10. The companion pin** `component-list-family-typed-members.pin.test.ts` — §1 parse-to-identity with the shared defs, §2 code AND path (arm issues for the two unions), §3 def identity through `._zod.def`, §4 the D3 registration; consistent with the schema as diffed; the `columns` cases go with the hold. **11. The kit** — D3 entry `ui-object-grid-kanban-calendar-list-members-typed` (D3 only, no conversion, reason recorded) and its generated registry region (text-identical to the entry file); rationale fragment order 66, equal to #21547's `page-requires-non-compiled-kind-refused` (equal orders render in id order per the header; the duplicates 56 / 60 / 62 pre-exist on `main`); `check:migration-registry` runs in `Lint & Repo Gates`, success. RIGHT in form; the entry's text does not name `options`, so only the four texts in ①1 move. **12. RIGHT. **13. Comment-only edits** — the `KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPES` docblock adds `ai:chat_window` (review `5965171663` ①10); the `ObjectGridPropsParsed` docblock now names the three defaults (`navigation`'s, `selection.type`, a column's `prefix.type`), which is accurate. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

**Level and arm RIGHT; one migration row WRONG on a fact.** `.changeset/21464-component-props-list-family-typed.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `feat(spec)!:`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (also PR body line 2), the BREAKING banner with the launch-window `minor` sentence, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered`, the new id), a FROM → TO table, the measured census, "Deployed metadata was not measured". `Check Changeset` is success, and the dev's `check-changeset-no-major` / `check-adr-0087-registration` / `check-widening-tells` readings (9 T1 tells at the lane's keys inside a former universal acceptor, the shape the gate rules a true refusal — declare `yes`) agree with the text, as #21445's did. The row "`object-grid` a column key the grid never reads, such as `editable` or `options` — delete the key" ships to consumers as `CHANGELOG.md` and tells an upgrading author to delete a key that changes the group headers a grouped grid draws; it and the "16 column keys the grid never reads" sentence are corrected in the same round as ①1 (right for `editable`, wrong for `options`). Observation, carried from `5963877733` ②: a bullet describes the enumeration pin, a test, in release prose.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0] (A3 versus the census) — contract matter; the seat's answer `5966636964` is applied as written.** Option A with one test. The test is met on `columns[].options` (①1) and not met on `editable` (①1) or on the `fields` object entries (①2). So eight of the nine narrowings stand on the seat's reading — a fixture probing a value the renderer drops, skips, diagnoses or refuses is not a working writer — and `object-grid` `columns` is held (option C for `columns`) pending the seat's ruling on the objectui read.
